Chambishi Copper Smelter Ltd Announces Major Expansion to Boost Output in Zambia

Chambishi Copper Smelter Ltd has unveiled plans for a significant expansion of its copper processing facilities in Zambia’s Copperbelt Province, aiming to increase its annual output and reinforce Zambia’s status as Africa’s second-largest copper producer. The company, which operates one of the region’s leading smelting plants, will invest approximately $190 million in new equipment, enhanced processing lines, and environmental upgrades over the next two years.

At a press briefing on Thursday, Chambishi Copper Smelter Ltd’s Managing Director, Joseph Mwila, said the expansion will lift the plant’s blister copper production capacity by 40%, from 250,000 tonnes to 350,000 tonnes per year by the end of 2026. “This investment demonstrates our confidence in Zambia’s mining sector and our commitment to supporting the government’s drive to increase beneficiation and value addition within the country,” Mwila stated.

The expansion will include the installation of a state-of-the-art oxygen-enriched furnace, improved sulphur capture systems for environmental compliance, and a new concentrate handling facility. According to the company, these upgrades are expected to enhance operating efficiency while reducing emissions, aligning with Zambia’s environmental regulations and global sustainability trends.

Industry analysts have welcomed the move, noting that increased local processing capacity comes at a time of robust global demand for copper, driven by the renewable energy and electric vehicle sectors. “Chambishi’s decision to expand is timely, given the persistent supply deficits in the copper market,” said Ruth Lungu, a mining analyst at Lusaka-based consultancy Katanga Resources. “It will also help Zambia capture more value from its mineral resources and create skilled jobs.”

The expansion is projected to create around 400 direct jobs during the construction phase and 120 permanent positions once operational, according to the company. In addition, the project is expected to generate increased business for suppliers and contractors in the Copperbelt region.

Zambia Chamber of Mines President, Daniel Sikaonga, commented, “We commend Chambishi Copper Smelter Ltd for this bold step, which aligns with the government’s target of raising annual copper output to 3 million tonnes by 2032. Expansions like these are critical for the long-term competitiveness of the Zambian mining industry.”

Chambishi Copper Smelter Ltd’s investment comes amid a broader wave of mining sector optimism in Zambia, following recent reforms aimed at clarifying mining tax policies and improving regulatory certainty. Construction is slated to begin in the third quarter of 2024, with the expanded plant expected to become fully operational by late 2026.
